title: USB-C overview: choose power role, data capability and PD support
summary: Specify sink/source/dual-role power behavior, data generation and Power Delivery support separately before selecting a port circuit.
applies_to: USB-C receptacles on end products; cables and adapters need their own requirements.
required_inputs: Power role, data role/rate, voltage/current budget and cable types
Connector, controller, startup supply and required modes
verification: Record supported modes and applicable specification editions; read only the matching patterns.
limitations: A connector does not imply SuperSpeed, USB4, PD or a particular power rating.

title: USB-C specification selection and edition tracking
summary: Track Type-C connector/CC requirements, USB data requirements and USB PD requirements as separate documents, with applicable amendments and compliance tests.
applies_to: Selecting normative references for a defined USB-C product.
required_inputs: Product roles and supported USB/PD features
Selected controller's supported revisions and relevant USB-IF test documents
verification: Record editions and section references in the project; verify release updates before design release.
limitations: The recorded Type-C 2.5 and PD 3.2 Version 1.2 listings are release pointers, not fully ingested specifications or proof of conformance.

title: USB-C fixed 5 V sink CC pattern
summary: For a fixed sink receptacle, provide independent Rd termination on CC1 and CC2. Nominal discrete Rd is 5.1 kOhm; review specified tolerance and any integrated termination.
applies_to: A non-PD fixed sink receptacle; optional USB 2.0 data is a separate path.
required_inputs: CC implementation, current entitlement and load budget
Controller integrated Rd/dead-battery behavior, if present
verification: Verify independent CC paths in both plug orientations and limit load to the detected or otherwise permitted current.
limitations: Two Rd resistors do not negotiate higher voltage or authorize 3 A. Do not parallel extra Rd with a controller's integrated terminations.

pattern.diagram:
CC1 -- Rd1 -- GND
CC2 -- Rd2 -- GND
VBUS -> reviewed input power path -> load
Rd may be integrated; CC1 and CC2 stay separate.
placement: Place CC circuitry near the receptacle.
routing: Keep each CC path independent and include protection loading in the review.
return_path: Connect receptacle ground contacts to the system reference.
pitfalls: Do not join CC1 and CC2 or use a single shared Rd.

title: USB-C source with controlled VBUS pattern
summary: Advertise only available current through CC source behavior and enable VBUS through an appropriate controlled power path after valid attachment.
applies_to: A fixed source receptacle; PD sources additionally need PD negotiation.
required_inputs: Available source power, CC controller and switch protections
Attach/detach policy, VBUS discharge and fault behavior
verification: Verify unattached, attached, detached and fault states with both orientations; measure current limiting and VBUS behavior.
limitations: An always-on supply and sink Rd resistors are not a source implementation. Controller example capacitances are not universal port limits.

pattern.diagram:
CC1/CC2 <-> source CC controller -> power-switch control
Supply -> protected switch -> receptacle VBUS
placement: Place the controller and power switch near the connector boundary.
routing: Size the supply path from current, loss and thermal budgets.
return_path: Keep power and signal return paths connected with deliberate geometry.
pitfalls: Do not advertise current the supply, connector or PCB cannot sustain.

title: USB-C dual power role and data role review
summary: Use supported role-control behavior for a dual-role port; power role and data role can be managed separately when the implementation supports it.
required_inputs: Controller features, allowed power/data roles and startup state
Power-path interlocks, firmware configuration and dead-battery supply
verification: Exercise each supported role, startup without a battery and rejected/accepted role changes.
limitations: Do not build DRP by fitting static Rp and Rd together. A CC-only controller does not supply a USB PD policy engine.

title: USB-C VCONN and cable capability review
summary: Determine whether the design must supply VCONN and discover cable capabilities. Cable power rating and supported data rates are separate properties.
applies_to: Ports using electronically marked or active cables and PD cable discovery.
required_inputs: Cable classes, current/data requirements and controller VCONN support
verification: Check orientation-controlled VCONN, cable discovery and behavior with lower-capability cables.
limitations: Do not treat both CC pins as permanent power outputs or assume any USB-C cable supports 5 A, EPR or the chosen data rate.

title: USB-C orientation, power-state and compliance review
summary: Test supported plug orientations, cable classes, power states and data modes. Separate functional tests from the applicable USB-IF compliance program.
applies_to: Review and qualification planning for a selected USB-C product.
required_inputs: Supported modes, cable matrix, controller configuration and specification/test editions
verification: Read schematic nets and inspect layout; test attach/detach, board-off behavior, power limits and data in both orientations.
Record PD negotiation/fault behavior where applicable, electrical test results and unresolved findings.
limitations: ERC/DRC, successful charging, or a controller's certification does not establish end-product compliance.
